title: Varnish Cache Architecture and Operations Review

questions.question: What is Varnish's primary role in a web request path?
options: A durable system of record for user accounts
An HTTP reverse proxy that can serve reusable responses from memory
A browser-side JavaScript database
A message broker for background jobs
questions.explanation: Varnish sits between clients and an HTTP origin. It can reuse cacheable responses, reducing origin work and response latency.

questions.question: Why should an authenticated account page normally return pass from vcl_recv?
options: Varnish cannot forward Authorization headers
Passing makes the response immutable
A shared object must not be reused across user identities unless isolation is explicitly proven
Authenticated responses are always larger than memory
questions.explanation: Passing authenticated traffic keeps user-specific responses out of the shared cache. Hashing only the URL could otherwise leak one user's representation to another.

questions.question: What is the likely effect of hashing every analytics and experiment cookie?
options: The cache gains a single universal object
Object variants fragment and the hit rate usually falls
The origin no longer receives misses
Cache-Control becomes unnecessary
questions.explanation: Each distinct cookie combination can create another object identity. High-cardinality dimensions turn reusable responses into mostly cold variants.

questions.question: Which VCL subroutine is the main place to decide whether an incoming request should pass or proceed to cache lookup?
options: vcl_recv
vcl_deliver
vcl_backend_error
vcl_fini
questions.explanation: vcl_recv handles the incoming request before lookup. Method, authorization, cookies, and routing can determine pass, hash, pipe, purge, or a synthetic response.

questions.question: An object is 90 seconds beyond TTL, the origin is slow, and the object has 300 seconds of grace. What can Varnish do?
options: Serve the bounded stale object while a refresh is attempted
Convert the response into a permanent redirect
Write the object to the origin database
Guarantee the origin is healthy
questions.explanation: Grace extends how long an expired object may be used under defined conditions. This can protect clients and the origin during slow refreshes, but it does not make stale content universally acceptable.

questions.question: How does request coalescing reduce a cache stampede?
options: It sends every waiter to a different backend
It disables cache lookup for popular URLs
It lets one request fetch an object while equivalent waiters reuse the result or receive grace
It makes TTL infinite
questions.explanation: Collapsing equivalent misses prevents thousands of clients from starting the same origin work when one popular object expires.

questions.question: Why is a broad fleet-wide purge risky during peak traffic?
options: It changes GET requests into POST requests
It can make many popular objects cold simultaneously and create an origin surge
It disables backend health probes forever
It duplicates every cache key
questions.explanation: Invalidating a large working set removes origin shielding at once. Versioned URLs, targeted bans, soft purge, and staged rollout can bound the refill wave.

questions.question: Which evidence best explains a falling Varnish hit rate?
options: Only total server CPU
A generic benchmark from another website
Request-level hit/pass/miss reasons, object age, cache key dimensions, eviction, and origin response headers
The number of lines in the VCL file
questions.explanation: Varnish logs and cache metrics reveal whether requests pass, miss, fragment, expire, or evict. A hit-rate percentage alone does not identify the policy or capacity cause.
